subject: Annual commitment liquidity playbook and invoice cadence
messages:
From: Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@greenlinelabs.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jared Lutz <jared.lutz@greenlinelabs.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Annual commitment — proposed invoice ladder and monthly mini-invoices

Hi Ava,

Thanks for the intro earlier — we’ve run the numbers and Greenline is ready to lock in a 12-month committed spend with Redwood. Finance asked me to confirm a practical invoice cadence that lines up with our internal cash-flow windows. Quick summary of what we need: 

- Initial deposit to activate committed capacity (one-time).
- A predictable, low-friction recurring invoice cadence (we prefer monthly mini-invoices rather than quarterly lumps) so our AP system can process smaller payments automatically.
- Country-specific VAT handling: EU entities will need VAT invoice lines separated per entity; some EU subsidiaries will use reverse charge where applicable.

Attached is a simple cashflow ask (Greenline_request_cashflow.xlsx) showing our preferred months for payments and expected bank remit dates. Can your team propose a compliant schedule that preserves Redwood’s drawdown tracking and audit trail? We’d like to finalize by next week so Procurement can raise the PO.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-min call if easier.

— Samantha
Samantha Reed
Head of Finance Operations
Greenline Labs

Attachments: Greenline_request_cashflow.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@greenlinelabs.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 08:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Annual commitment — proposed invoice ladder and monthly mini-invoices

Samantha — thanks for the clear ask and the attachment. We can accommodate monthly "mini-invoices" for the year while still tracking usage against an annual committed balance. High-level proposal below; I’ve attached a draft ladder (2028-07-19-Redwood-Invoice-Ladder-draft.xlsx) for your AP team to review.

Proposed flow (summary):
- Invoice 1 (Activation): initial deposit for X USD — invoiced on contract signature. This posts against the committed balance.
- Months 1–11: monthly mini-invoices (non-cumulative) that withdraw pre-agreed increments from the committed balance. Each mini-invoice references the master commitment ID and remaining committed balance.
- Final Reconciliation: month 12 — a reconciliation invoice that true-ups usage vs committed spend; any shortfall is invoiced, any overage becomes refundable credit or applied to next term per contract terms.

VAT handling: we need to confirm the billing entity per invoice (Redwood, Redwood EU subsidiary, or Redwood US) to determine VAT treatment. If Greenline’s EU subsidiary is the legal customer and provides a valid VAT ID, we can apply reverse-charge on EU invoices where eligible — otherwise we’ll issue standard VAT invoices from the EU entity.

Operational asks for next steps: 
1) Confirm billing entity and VAT ID for each payee line in the attached EU_entity_mapping.csv (we can accept this via reply).
2) Confirm whether Greenline prefers invoices on the 1st of month or on your stated remit dates in the spreadsheet.
3) Provide PO number format so we can include it on every mini-invoice.

Connor and Kimberly are looped for ledger and tax handling; Kimberly will provide the VAT playbook and amendment language for the SOW so legal/ops are aligned. If this looks good I’ll prepare an amendment and DocuSign link for signature.

Best,
Ava Chen
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 2028-07-19-Redwood-Invoice-Ladder-draft.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Jared Lutz <jared.lutz@greenlinelabs.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>, Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@greenlinelabs.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Annual commitment — proposed invoice ladder and monthly mini-invoices

Thanks Ava — a couple clarifications from Procurement: 
- Greenline will require separate invoices per legal entity for EU payees — we can supply the EU VAT IDs and remittance bank details once you confirm invoice references.
- For reverse charge: we’ll attach VAT IDs, but Procurement needs a short vendor attestation stating when Redwood will reverse-charge vs collect VAT (we need that for our AP feed).

Attaching a mapping file (EU_entity_mapping.csv) with the five EU subsidiaries that will be billed separately. Samantha — can you confirm the preferred invoice date? Our AP team likes invoices dated on the 1st but our treasury remit windows are the 5th and 20th of each month.

— Jared
Greenline Labs

Attachments: EU_entity_mapping.csv (csv)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@greenlinelabs.com>, Jared Lutz <jared.lutz@greenlinelabs.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Jul 2028 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Annual commitment — proposed invoice ladder and monthly mini-invoices

Folks — looping in the tax and collections perspective so we have a single operational playbook. Key points and recommended wording for the amendment: 

1) Invoice structure:
- Activation invoice (single) from Redwood, Inc. (US entity) for the initial deposit — references Commitment ID DL-78902-GREEN.
- Monthly mini-invoices issued per legal customer entity. For EU subsidiaries we will issue separate invoices from Redwood EU (where required) with VAT lines. If the EU subsidiary provides a valid VAT ID and the supply is B2B, we will include the reverse-charge statement on the invoice and leave VAT at 0% with the note: "Reverse charge applies per Article X — customer liable for VAT."

2) Drawdown tracking / ledger: 
- Each mini-invoice includes: invoice_date, invoice_number, commitment_id, period_start, period_end, amount_invoiced, remaining_commitment_balance. This makes automated reconciliation straightforward for both teams.

3) PO and bank remit fields: include PO number, billing entity address, and templated bank instructions per legal entity (we’ll attach the bank remit CSV).

4) Timeline & triggers: 
- Target: activation invoice within 48 hours of DocuSign execution.
- Monthly mini-invoices generated on the 1st of each month; remits expected on the 5th or 20th per Greenline’s remit preference.

I’ve drafted amendment language and a document we can route via DocuSign: amendment_draft.docx. I recommend we handle the EU VAT attestation as a one-page appendix that Greenline’s AP signs off on (satisfies their internal control).

If Connor is good on ledger fields I’ll publish the amendment and route for signature.

Thanks — I’ll also add a short sample CSV schema for the invoice ladder to the internal drive.

— Kimberly Park
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: amendment_draft.docx (word)

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@greenlinelabs.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Final: commitment liquidity playbook & DocuSign link

Samantha — confirming next steps and links so Procurement can raise the PO: 

1) We will proceed with the activation invoice from Redwood, Inc. (US) upon signature. Monthly mini-invoices will be generated on the 1st of each month and will reference Commitment ID DL-78902-GREEN and the remaining committed balance.
2) For EU subsidiaries: please reply with VAT IDs in the same CSV format (we received EU_entity_mapping.csv) — once we receive and validate the VAT IDs we’ll apply reverse-charge indicators where eligible. If reverse-charge is not applicable we’ll issue a VAT invoice from Redwood EU.
3) DocuSign link to amendment + SOW: https://app.docusign.net/Redwood/EM-2028-07-23-amendment (please sign to trigger the activation invoice).
4) Please provide your PO number (or PO format) and confirm whether Greenline wants remits on the 5th or the 20th.

For transparency, attached is the signed SOW we have on file (Redwood_SOW_signed.pdf) — activation will follow immediately after amendment signature and payment of the deposit.

If you’d like a 15-min handoff with our billing/collections team I’ll schedule Connor to walk through the invoice CSV schema and bank remit matrix.

Appreciate the prompt turnaround — we’ll queue the DocuSign today.

Best regards,
Ava Chen
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_SOW_signed.pdf (pdf)
